Subject: Security exhibit: evidence prioritization & 'inspection-lite' proposal

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for sending over Aurelia's initial MSA redlines last week. I pulled together a focused counter-proposal for the Security Exhibit so we can keep procurement moving while minimizing operational overhead on both sides. Key points in the attached doc:

- "Inspection-lite" option: scoped read-only evidence snapshots vs full inspection (short list of artifacts + remote sampling).
- Pen test notification window options (30/14/7 days) and a recommended 30-day maximum with a rolling 24-hour staging access window for controlled tests.
- SOC 2 mapping appendix: which assertions we can provide evidence for vs evidence that requires on-prem or privileged access.
- Evidence cadence proposals: quarterly report + on-demand artifact package for audits.

We tried to be prescriptive about what "evidence snapshots" include (control IDs, logs extract, diagram) so your security team can triage quickly. If this approach looks workable, we can convert the redlines into tracked changes in your MSA and propose a handshake process for evidence delivery.

I've attached Aurelia_MSA_redlines_v3.docx and a short PDF with inline comments. Vanessa and Karthik are looped in for technical/legal clarifications.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync this week (15–20m) to confirm the inspection-lite scope and pen-test window.
2) If agreed, legal takes the tracked-change MSA back and we target a single pass to final redlines.

Available: Wed 9/2 11:00–13:00 PT, Thu 9/3 09:00–12:00 PT. Tell me what works for you.

Thanks,
Markus

Thanks for looping me in. Quick technical clarifications from security:

- Logs extract: we can provide token-level and api-gateway logs with a 90-day retention snapshot; for SOC 2 we usually supply aggregated access logs (UTC timestamps, request path, requester id) and a filtered sample (1–7 days) for the assertion period. We will not provide raw customer prompts or post-processed outputs unless contractually required; that needs an explicit data access clause.

- Inspection-lite: propose a three-bucket model:
  1) Artifact package (standard): SOC 2 report, diagram, config snapshot, access control list export (quarterly).
  2) Evidence snapshot (on-request): filtered logs, system config details, and a short replay script for repro (redacted). Delivery SLA: 5 business days.
  3) Privileged inspection: only for critical escalations or regulator requests; requires scoped creds and an agreed runbook.

- Pen test window: we agree 30 days is reasonable as a default; we can offer an expedited 14-day option for customers that can commit to a pre-authorized staging token and a constrained blast radius. Staging access would be a rolling 48-hour window that we can rotate creds for.

I added inline comments to the PDF for suggested redline language. From a risk perspective, we should:
- Keep data exfiltration tooling out of the default deliverables
- Limit privileged inspection to a named process with a legal attestation

If legal is comfortable with the proposed "artifact package + evidence snapshot" definitions, we can make the tracked-change MSA language explicit and provide procurement a timeline: 5 business days for legal review + 3 business days for operational coordination.

Happy to walk through on Thu 9/3 at 10:00 PT.

—Vanessa

Daniel/Team —

Couple of legal notes after reviewing Markus's doc and Vanessa's comments:

1) Evidence scope language: replace open-ended "provide logs" phrasing with a defined list and delivery SLA (we recommend the Evidence Snapshot bucket described by Vanessa with explicit control IDs).
2) Pen test indemnity: redraft to preserve typical vendor limitations (no access to customer PII), and require a scoping statement pre-test signed by both parties.
3) Audit rights: propose removing any clause that suggests unfettered on-site access; instead we should accept remote review with a limited privileged inspection process under a formal request and legal attestation.

I'll prepare tracked-change suggestions (legal) and attach a short cover note that procurement can rely on to speed review. If you want, I can send the tracked-change draft by end of day Thu so your procurement team has something to review Fri.
